## Types

### Fft

```odin
Fft :: struct {...}
```

A complex FFT of a fixed size whose only prime factors are 2, 3 and 5
(see `fft_fast_size_above`). Unnormalised both ways: the forward
transform uses e^(−2πi·kn/N), the inverse e^(+2πi·kn/N), and an inverse
after a forward multiplies by N. f32 data, twiddles computed in f64.

A transform can run in one call or in `fft_steps` pieces (one per radix
stage), to spread its cost over several audio blocks. Set up with
`fft_init`; free with `fft_destroy`. One transform at a time per Fft.
Fields are internal.

### Real_Fft

```odin
Real_Fft :: struct {
	size: int,
	half_bin: bool,
	split: bool,
	complex: Fft,
	twiddles: []complex64,
	twists: []complex64,
	time: []complex64,
	freq: []complex64,
}
```

An FFT of `size` real samples (even; size/2 a fast size), giving size/2
complex bins. Same conventions as `Fft` (unnormalised; inverse after
forward multiplies by `size`). Two spectrum layouts:

- Normal: bin k is X[k] for 1 ≤ k < size/2, and bin 0 packs DC (real
  part) with Nyquist (imaginary part).
- Half-bin (`half_bin`): bin k is the spectrum at k + ½, for 0 ≤ k <
  size/2: X[k+½] = Σ x[n]·e^(−2πi·(k+½)n/size). No packing; the bins sit
  symmetrically around the frequencies that matter (used by STFTs).

With `split`, the final (forward) or first (inverse) twiddle pass is done
in two halves, for one more step and smaller pieces. Laid out as
Signalsmith Linear's RealFFT, so ported code steps through it the same
way. Set up with `real_fft_init`; free with `real_fft_destroy`. Fields are
internal.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `size` |  |
| `half_bin` |  |
| `split` |  |
| `complex` |  |
| `twiddles` |  |
| `twists` | half-bin: e^(−2πi·n/size), applied to the input pairs |
| `time` |  |
| `freq` |  |

### One_Pole_Lowpass

```odin
One_Pole_Lowpass :: struct {
	cutoff: Smoothed_Value,
	g: f64,
	state: []f64,
	sample_rate: f64,
}
```

One-pole lowpass, topology-preserving transform (Zavalishin, "The Art of VA
Filter Design", ch. 3). Exactly -3.01 dB at cutoff thanks to prewarping.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `cutoff` | Hz |
| `g` | G = g / (1 + g), g = tan(pi fc / fs) |
| `state` | one per channel, allocated in prepare |
| `sample_rate` |  |

### Resampler_Quality

```odin
Resampler_Quality :: enum u8 {
	Low,
	Medium,
	High,
}
```

Interpolation quality: how much of the band is kept flat and how far
aliases are pushed down, at the cost of taps (multiply-adds) per output
sample and channel. Above speed 1 the filter widens by the speed, so the
taps grow with it. Medium suits clip playback; High suits offline work.

| Quality | Taps (speed ≤ 1) | Flat to (× Nyquist) | Aliases and images |
|---------|------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| Low     | 32               | 0.75                | below −60 dB       |
| Medium  | 80               | 0.85                | below −90 dB       |
| High    | 160              | 0.90                | below −120 dB      |

### Resampler

```odin
Resampler :: struct {...}
```

Converts a stream between sample rates, or plays it faster or slower
(varispeed), with bandlimited interpolation: each output sample is a
Kaiser-windowed sinc evaluated at its exact position between input
samples (Julius O. Smith's method). The speed may change on every call.

Output frame k is the input at time `k × speed` (summed over calls), with
no added delay; the resampler only needs to see a little input ahead
(`resampler_input_needed` says how much). Planar f32. Set up with
`resampler_init`, free with `resampler_destroy`. Fields are internal.

```odin
}
```

Per-sample parameter smoother. Nodes own one per smoothed parameter.
Advancing is per sample, so the result never depends on block boundaries.

| `target` | value being approached |
| `mode` |  |

### Stft_Spectrum

```odin
Stft_Spectrum :: enum u8 {
	Packed,
	Half_Bin,
	Unpacked,
}
```

How an `Stft` lays out its spectrum.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Packed` | fft_size/2 bins; bin 0 holds DC (real) and Nyquist (imaginary) |
| `Half_Bin` | fft_size/2 bins at k + ½ (see `Real_Fft`); suits spectral processing |
| `Unpacked` | fft_size/2 + 1 bins, Nyquist in its own bin |

```odin
Stft_Window :: enum u8 {
	Keep,
	Acg,
	Kaiser,
}
```

The window shape `stft_set_interval` builds.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Keep` | leave the windows as they are |
| `Acg` | approximate confined Gaussian |
| `Kaiser` | Kaiser, with a bandwidth chosen for the interval |

### Stft_Normalisation

```odin
Stft_Normalisation :: enum u8 {
	Round_Trip,
	Synthesis,
	None,
}
```

What output is divided by, so that analysis then synthesis gives back the
input whatever the windows and block positions.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Round_Trip` | analysis × synthesis windows (the default) |
| `Synthesis` | the synthesis window only |
| `None` | only the FFT's gain |

### Stft

```odin
Stft :: struct {...}
```

A short-time Fourier transform for spectral processing: write input,
analyse a block into spectra, change the spectra, synthesise them back,
read output. It normalises itself: output is divided by the sum of the
window products of the blocks that went into it, so analysis then
synthesis at a steady hop (not only the default interval) reconstructs
the input exactly, `stft_latency` minus one hop later when output is read
straight after synthesising. (With uneven hops the gain varies, exactly
as in Signalsmith Linear.)

Analysis and synthesis can also run in steps (`stft_analyse_steps`), to
spread their cost. Planar f32; nothing allocates after `stft_init`.
Fields are internal.

### Stft_Input

```odin
Stft_Input :: struct {
	pos: int,
	buffer: []f32,
}
```

An STFT's input history, which can be saved and swapped (as Signalsmith
Stretch does to re-analyse). Make one with `stft_input_make`. Fields are
internal.

### Stft_Output

```odin
Stft_Output :: struct {...}
```

An STFT's pending output, which can be saved and swapped. Make one with
`stft_output_make`. Fields are internal.

```odin
Stft_Settings :: struct {
	in_channels: int,
	out_channels: int,
	block: int,
	extra_history: int,
	interval: int,
	asymmetry: f64,
	fft_min_size: int,

```

| Field | Description |

| `block` | block (window) length in samples |
| `extra_history` | input kept beyond one block, for analysing in the past |
| `interval` | default hop; 0 = block/4 |
| `asymmetry` | window warp, −1..1; 0 = symmetric |
| `fft_min_size` | 0 = block |
| `spectrum` |  |
| `split` | allow analysing and synthesising in more, smaller steps |

### resampler_reset

```odin
resampler_reset :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Forgets all input: the next output frame is the next input frame,
preceded by silence.

### resampler_input_needed

```odin
resampler_input_needed :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler, out_frames: int, speed: f64) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Input frames to add before `out_frames` more output frames can be
produced at `speed` (0 if enough is buffered). For pull-style playback:
read this many frames, then call `resampler_process` once.

### resampler_process

```odin
resampler_process :: proc "contextless"(r: ^Resampler, input: [][]f32, output: [][]f32, speed: f64) -> (consumed: int, produced: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Resamples at `speed` input frames per output frame (> 0, at most
`max_speed`): takes frames from `input` (one slice per channel, all the
same length) and writes frames to `output` (likewise) until the input is
used up or the output is full. Returns how many frames were consumed and
produced. Never allocates.

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Moves the output position on by `samples`, clearing what it passes.

### stft_finish_output

```odin
stft_finish_output :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, strength: f32 = 1, offset: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). When no more synthesis is coming, lets the output taper to zero with
the windows rather than being scaled up as if blocks were just far apart.
Applies from `offset` samples ahead; `strength` 0..1.

### stft_analyse

```odin
stft_analyse :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, samples_in_past: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Analyses the latest block of input (or one ending `samples_in_past`
samples ago) into every channel's spectrum.

### stft_analyse_steps

```odin
stft_analyse_steps :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Steps an analysis takes (one per channel, or more with `split`).

### stft_analyse_step

```odin
stft_analyse_step :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, step: int, samples_in_past: int = 0)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of an analysis; run all of them in order.

### stft_synthesise

```odin
stft_synthesise :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Synthesises every channel's spectrum and adds the result to the
output at the current position.

### stft_synthesise_steps

```odin
stft_synthesise_steps :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft) -> int
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Steps a synthesis takes.

### stft_synthesise_step

```odin
stft_synthesise_step :: proc "contextless"(s: ^Stft, step: int)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Step `step` of a synthesis; run all of them in order.
